newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin urges new Chechen leader to rebuild ties.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin urges new Chechen leader to rebuild ties.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin appealed to the newly-elected leader of rebel Chechnya on Sunday for cooperation in rebuilding relations after a two-year war and said with goodwill all problems could be solved.

Yeltsin, in his first formal address to Aslan Maskhadov since his election victory last Monday, said the polls marked an important step on the road to "regulating" relations between Moscow and Grozny.
Yeltsin's note, issued by Interfax news agency, avoided any language that could be interpreted as a recognition of Chechen independence.

"(Improved relations) will require a great deal of time, goodwill and effort from all sides. I am convinced that only by the path of dialogue and cooperation can we solve all existing problems," Yeltsin said.

Yeltsin sent troops into Chechnya in December 1994 to try to crush Chechnya's drive to independence. The 21-month campaign proved disastrous for the Russian army and ended in a peace deal allowing elections, the withdrawal of Moscow's troops and deferral of the issue of sovereignty for five years.
Maskhadov, however, has said he will raise the issue of full independence quickly with the Kremlin.
Yeltsin, fearing Chechen independence could encourage separatism elsewhere in the vast and disparate Russian Federation, has said formal independence is out of the question.
Yeltsin had branded Chechen rebels bandits and criminals during the war in which thousands had been killed.

In Maskhadov, however, the Kremlin has a man they know is acceptable as a negotiating partner. He was the chief force in last year's peace talks, called after stunning rebel victories over Russian troops in the ruins of the capital, Grozny.
"I hope that your activity in this high post will be directed towards the establishment of peace and stability in the republic (and the)...reinforcement of ethnic accord," Yeltsin said.
"Electors see in your victory hopes of a good and just life. I believe that you can justify these hopes," Yeltsin said.
The note was handed to President Maskhakov in Grozny by Security Council Secretary Ivan Rybkin.
